sections.html:
Owners in Fort Worth have three ordinary choices: an all-cash bid, an agent listing, or a sale to an investor who will renovate. Paying cash buys you speed and certainty at some cost in price. Listing buys a larger audience at a cost in time.

The city is large and varied. It has 334,230 households, 56.7 percent of them owner occupied, and single-family homes cover 24.1 percent of the land. A bungalow near downtown, a ranch house on the far north side and a newer subdivision near Alliance are three different sales with three different buyer pools, so ask any buyer how they priced your specific house, not just the area.

  • Cash offer: often as-is, with no lender appraisal and a date you negotiate.
  • Agent listing: staging, photos, showings, and repair negotiation after the inspection.
  • Investor purchase: common for dated homes, rentals with tenants, or houses with code or foundation concerns.

Whichever you choose, ask for an itemized estimate of your take-home.

sections.h2: Fort Worth's size and your price
sections.html:
Fort Worth is home to over one million people and was the fastest-growing large city in the nation, gaining 170,237 residents between 2010 and 2020. Projections reach 1,306,400 by 2050. Steady demand helps a seller. Vacant land makes up 37.6 percent of the city's land use, though, and new construction on it gives buyers alternatives to your house.

The city is served by 13 independent school districts, so the district name on a house matters as much as the city name. Check the district for your exact address before you advertise.

An unpaid balance for the year stays with the house regardless of who holds title when the bill comes. The county tax office can print a statement that shows each unit's share, which matters because school, county, city and special district bills vary by address. Penalties begin in February and keep climbing into summer.

Late-payment charges on Texas property tax
ChargeRule
First penaltySix percent, added the first day of February
InterestOne percent a month with no cap
Higher penaltyTwelve percent once July begins
Collection lawyerUp to 20 percent extra if the unit has a contract

Any balance is paid by the closing agent, so get the payoff figure early.

For the most part, no. A homestead exemption stops when you stop owning. The one carry-over is the school tax ceiling for older or disabled owners, which can follow you in proportion to a new Texas homestead.

  • After the exemption is first claimed, a homestead's appraised value can rise by no more than 10 percent a year.
  • Any local taxing unit may adopt an exemption of up to 20 percent of value.
  • Owners with a disability rating may get partial or full relief on the home.

Let the appraisal district know about the sale so your account closes properly, and keep your final tax statement for your records in case a question comes up later.

All three have a workable path. Heirs can use a muniment of title to pass a house when no administration is needed. A lender generally waits until a loan is more than 120 days late, and the default notice includes time to cure, which leaves room to sell instead of losing the house.

For a rented house, many buyers will take the property with the lease intact, which can spare you an eviction. If you need it empty, the process starts with written notice and then moves to justice court.

In all three cases, tell buyers up front. A cash buyer who knows about an heir's signature, a default date or a tenant can price the situation. A buyer who learns about it at the end tends to cut the offer or walk.

The clerk of the county where the land is located records the deed. Your closing agent normally submits it, and the fee is taken from closing funds, which you can confirm on the settlement statement. A notary or similar officer has to acknowledge the signature first.

  • Ask your lender for a payoff letter.
  • Find the last recorded deed and releases of any old liens.
  • Run a lien search for judgments and tax liens.
  • Leave keys, garage openers and warranty papers for the new owner.

sections.h2: Local features that help a listing
sections.html:
Parks and open space draw buyers. The city maintains 300 parks covering 13,000 acres, and the Fort Worth Nature Center and Refuge spans 3,621 acres with more than 20 miles of trails. Mention the nearest park, trail or transit route in your listing.

Large public projects, including a $700 million convention center expansion, can shift traffic and nearby demand over several years. Ask a local agent or the city planning office what is under way near your street before you set a price, and keep records of any recent upgrades for the buyer.

sections.h2: What the closing table looks like
sections.html:
At signing you will receive a settlement statement that lists every dollar. The sale price sits at the top and the deductions follow: the lender's payoff, your share of the tax, title and recording charges, and whatever the contract assigns to you. The remainder is your net. Check each line against the contract, and ask the closing agent about any entry you cannot identify.

A rental sale may add prorated rent and the tenant's deposit to the statement. An inherited house requires everyone with signing authority over the estate to attend or send signed paperwork beforehand.

Build your move around funding. Proceeds typically arrive the same day or the next business day after recording, so hold off on any purchase that depends on that money until it is in your account.

A fast sale starts with a tidy file. Before asking for bids, round up your deed, a contact at the lender who can issue the payoff, this year's tax statement and any receipts for roof, foundation or plumbing jobs. Then walk the house with a notepad and write down every defect you already know about. An inspector will uncover them regardless, and a list in your own hand makes a buyer trust the rest of what you say.

Judge each bid on four points: the amount that reaches you, the closing date, the repairs you are expected to make, and who covers title and recording costs. Insist on the bid in writing with an expiration date. Once you accept, an escrow officer orders the title search, clears any liens and sets a signing time. You sign with a notary, the loan is retired, and the remainder is wired to you.

faqs.q: Can I sell in Fort Worth while a mortgage is open?
faqs.a: Yes. Your lender is paid first at the closing table and the remainder is yours. Request a payoff letter that stays valid through your closing date.

faqs.q: Which clerk records my Fort Worth deed?
faqs.a: The clerk for the county that holds the lot. Your tax bill names the county, so check it before you file.

faqs.q: Must I fix things before a cash sale in Fort Worth?
faqs.a: No, as-is buyers take the house in its current state. Roof, foundation and plumbing issues lower the offer, so set it beside a listing net after repairs.

faqs.q: Who pays unpaid Fort Worth property tax at a sale?
faqs.a: The closing agent clears the balance from your proceeds. Ask the county tax office for a statement before you sign.

faqs.q: Can a Fort Worth rental be sold with the tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers accept the lease. If you want the house empty, written notice and a justice court case come first.
